_comment: One drill per coaching cue. At the end of a session the summary suggests at most two, for the corrections that actually repeated, and explains why each was chosen.

plant_behind.name: Plant-and-strike gates
plant_behind.setup: Put two cones a boot-width apart, level with a stationary ball, on your standing-foot side.
plant_behind.how: Walk in, place your standing foot between the cones, then strike. Start at half pace.
plant_behind.why: It fixes where your standing foot lands, so it ends up level with the ball rather than behind it.

plant_ahead.name: Plant-and-strike gates
plant_ahead.setup: Put two cones a boot-width apart, level with a stationary ball, on your standing-foot side.
plant_ahead.how: Walk in, place your standing foot between the cones, then strike. Start at half pace.
plant_ahead.why: It fixes where your standing foot lands, so it stops overrunning the ball.

leaning_back.name: Chest-over-the-ball volleys
leaning_back.setup: Stand a step behind a stationary ball.
leaning_back.how: Strike at half power, freezing after contact with your chest over the ball and your shoulders ahead of your hips.
leaning_back.why: Freezing after each strike trains you to finish over the ball, which keeps shots low.

short_follow_through.name: Land-on-your-kicking-foot finish
short_follow_through.setup: A stationary ball and a target a few metres away (wall, net or cone).
short_follow_through.how: After each strike, keep swinging through and land on your kicking foot, one step past where the ball was.
short_follow_through.why: Landing on the kicking foot forces a full follow-through toward the target.

short_backswing.name: Pendulum swings
short_backswing.how: Draw the kicking leg back until your heel comes up toward your backside, pause, then swing through and strike.
short_backswing.why: A fuller backswing gives the leg room to build speed before contact.

stiff_standing_leg.name: Soft-knee balance strikes
stiff_standing_leg.how: Plant with a slightly bent standing knee and hold your balance for two seconds after each strike.
stiff_standing_leg.why: A soft standing knee keeps you balanced through the strike.

ball_too_far.name: Every-step dribble lane
ball_too_far.setup: Mark a straight lane about 10 m long with two cones.
ball_too_far.how: Dribble down the lane touching the ball on every step, keeping it within one step of your feet. Walk, then jog.
ball_too_far.why: Touching on every step keeps the ball close, which is what the session measured as the main issue.

lost_control.name: Speed-ladder dribbling
lost_control.how: Dribble the lane at 50%, then 70%, then 85% pace. Only go faster when the ball stays close at the slower pace.
lost_control.why: Building pace step by step finds the speed at which you still keep control.

heavy_touches.name: Cushion-touch wall passes
heavy_touches.setup: Stand 3 to 4 m from a wall.
heavy_touches.how: Pass against the wall and cushion the return with the inside of your foot, so the ball stops within a step. Then pass again.
heavy_touches.why: Cushioning a moving ball trains soft touches that stay within a step.

few_touches.name: Touch-count dribble
few_touches.how: Dribble between the cones counting touches. Try to add one touch each length at the same pace.
few_touches.why: Counting touches builds the habit of touching the ball more often.

upright.name: Low-stance cone weave
upright.setup: Six cones in a line, 1.5 m apart.
upright.how: Weave through the cones with your knees bent and your hips low, as if sitting slightly.
upright.why: Weaving tight cones is much easier from a low stance, so it builds that habit.

toe_pokes.name: Inside-outside taps
toe_pokes.setup: A ball at your feet in a small space.
toe_pokes.how: Move the ball side to side with the inside of one foot, then the outside, without using your toes. Add forward movement once it feels smooth.
toe_pokes.why: It builds control with the side of the foot, which is more reliable than the toes.

one_foot.name: Weaker-foot only lane
one_foot.how: Dribble the lane using only your less-used foot, at a comfortable pace.
one_foot.why: Dedicated weaker-foot reps are the quickest way to use both feet in real play.

contact_laces.name: Toes-down laces strikes
contact_laces.setup: A stationary ball; mark the laces area of your boot with a strip of tape if that helps.
contact_laces.how: Point your toes down and lock the ankle before the swing. Strike the middle of the ball with the laces at half power.
contact_laces.why: Practising a locked, toes-down foot makes the laces meet the ball instead of the toe or the side of the foot.

contact_inside.name: Side-foot finishing gates
contact_inside.setup: Set two cones 1 m apart as a small goal, 6 to 8 m away, and a stationary ball.
contact_inside.how: Turn your kicking foot out so the inside faces the target, keep the ankle firm, and pass the ball through the gate. Follow through toward the gate.
contact_inside.why: Aiming at a narrow gate rewards a clean inside-of-the-foot contact.

contact_outside.name: Outside-foot flicks to a wall
contact_outside.setup: Stand 3 m from a wall with the ball slightly in front of your kicking foot.
contact_outside.how: Point your toes slightly in and strike the ball with the outside of your foot at half power. Control the rebound and repeat.
contact_outside.why: Short, repeated outside-foot contacts build the ankle position the outside-foot shot needs.
